claim_objects.claim_text: A Johnson County, Texas sheriff's deputy used Flock Safety's nationwide network on May 9, 2025 while seeking a woman associated with a reported self-managed abortion.
claim_objects.claim_scope: Existence, logged reason, and scale of the Flock search event.

claim_objects.claim_text: The public purpose descriptions include a contemporaneous abortion-specific search reason and a later welfare/safety characterization.
claim_objects.claim_scope: Purpose descriptions only; does not determine subjective motive.

source_objects.transport_log: Reports Columbus Division of Police audit logs showing the Johnson County search, its abortion-specific reason, and nationwide network access.
Independent FOIA-based confirmation of the May 9, 2025 Johnson County query and scope reaching 6,809 networks and 83,345 cameras.
Flock publicly characterizes the Johnson County search as an effort to locate a woman whose family feared she was hurt.

transport_result: PASS — retrospective audit records and independent public-record reporting expose the search event and nationwide reach.
claim_provenance_result: PASS — the event description, logged abortion-specific reason, and later welfare/safety characterization have identifiable public provenance.
applicability_result: HOLD — cross-agency and cross-jurisdictional authority remain unresolved by the protocol; system-wide disparity cannot be inferred from one event.
conflicts: Contemporaneous search log used abortion-specific language while later public explanations characterized the objective as welfare/safety; protocol records DRIFT and does not resolve motive.
